Done. `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint src/app/sections/hero --max-warnings=0` and `npm run build` all pass.

**What I changed** (only `src/app/sections/hero/`):

1. **Wordmark now scales with the headline** (the tablet + mobile warning). It was `h-7 w-[157px]`, hard-locked at every width, while `--text-display-xl` is `clamp(2.75rem, 7.5vw, 6.75rem)` — so at 768/390 the tag kept its desktop size and outgrew its own headline (0.38 / 0.54 of the longest line vs the 0.21 the 1440 frame draws). The Title frame now carries `font-size: var(--text-display-xl)`, and the wordmark is `calc(var(--hero-wordmark-ratio) * 1em)` with `--hero-wordmark-ratio: 1.4537` (= 157/108, the ratio Figma draws) and `height: auto`. That resolves to exactly 157px at 1440, ~84px at 768, ~64px at 390.

2. **Feathered legibility wash behind the lead, below 992px only** (the other tablet + mobile warning). Two earlier iterations tried to solve this by *moving* the block and neither position exists at these widths; re-anchoring the vessel doesn't help either, because the raster is 1.418:1 against a portrait stage so `object-fit: cover` crops horizontally only and `object-position` has no vertical effect there. So `.lead::before` paints a radial wash of the surface colour (`rgb(var(--white-rgb) / 0.68)` → 0 at 76%) inset by `--space-xlg`, fully feathered out inside its own bleed — no panel edge. Hard-gated off at ≥992px so the drawn desktop frame is untouched.

3. **Token hygiene:** `lg:mt-37` → `lg:mt-[var(--space-6xl)]` (148px) and `lg:mt-24` → `lg:mt-[var(--space-4xl)]` (96px). Same computed values — both are literal spec numbers with existing named tokens — now referencing the tokens.

**Two issues I could not act on:**

- The CRITICAL hero-imagery tone is confirmed at the source: Figma node `247:655` has **two** image fills, and the opaque top one (`9f1c066f…`, with exposure +0.06 / contrast +0.04) is what renders — the build carries the *lower* fill (`b7f71aa1…`). Fixing it means re-exporting the flattened asset, and binary assets are off-limits this pass (any write is auto-reverted, which would leave a broken `src`). This needs an asset-level fix outside the section pass.
- The Exposure/Matter `size-adjust` fallback faces live in the shared `globals.css`, which another agent owns — flagged for the shared-file follow-up, as the reviewer noted.
